Subject: BrightCo MSA — output entitlement & modeling-data carveouts

Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal has flagged two material items in the MSA/order form we need to resolve before procurement can proceed: output ownership and any allowance to use customer content for model training. BrightCo cannot accept language that assigns upstream ownership of model outputs or permits unilateral retraining on our customer data.

High level asks from our side:
- Customer retains exclusive rights to product output (generated content) for our commercial use.
- No use of customer content for model retraining or gradient updates unless we explicitly opt in via a separate addendum and defined compensation.
- If Redwood needs telemetry/feedback to operate the service, it should be limited and scoped with retention limits and attestations that no PII is used for training.

Attached is our redlined MSA (BrightCo_MSA_redlines_v1.docx). Please confirm next steps and a timeline — procurement is on a tight quarter close.

Best,
Emma Law
Senior Counsel, BrightCo

Thanks Emma — received and understood. Laura/Ben, looping you in to determine a pragmatic path. Short summary of what BrightCo is asking and our immediate thoughts:

1) Output ownership: BrightCo requests exclusive rights to generated output. Our standard position has been to grant customers broad rights to use outputs while retaining internal rights to service delivery and model improvements. We can propose a non-exclusive perpetual license to outputs for BrightCo's commercial use, plus an explicit carveout that Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified outputs for delivering the service.

2) Training/use of customer content: BrightCo wants a hard opt-in for model retraining. We can accept an express opt-in for retraining (separate addendum + credits) while allowing limited telemetry/feedback (logs, error traces) for operational stability under strict retention and PII redaction.

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
- 6/13: Redwood legal to provide proposed clause language and a short redline.
- 6/14: BrightCo to review and confirm or propose edits.
- 6/18: Finalize language and route to procurement/DocuSign.

Attaching a brief suggested clause set (Redwood_proposed_clause_v2.docx) for legal review. Laura — can you draft language that implements the opt-in retraining guardrail + a scoped telemetry exception (30 day retention, no PII, only aggregated model-improvement metadata)? Ben — I recommend we keep commercial terms (credits for retrain) as a redline negotiation lever.

Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts

Jonas / Ben — I reviewed Emma's redline and Jonas' suggested approach. Below are redline notes and a compromise clause we can push.

Redline notes summary:
- We should avoid "exclusive ownership" language for outputs — it creates carry risks for our service model and downstream tooling. Instead, propose: "Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, transferable right to use and exploit Outputs." This gives BrightCo commercial freedom while preserving Redwood's right to operate the service.
- For training: propose explicit two-track language: (a) Operational telemetry: Redwood may collect ephemeral telemetry strictly to maintain and operate the service (defined categories only, retained for 30 days, PII-stripped). This telemetry is not used for model retraining. (b) Retraining: any use of Customer Content for model retraining or creating new model weights requires a separate written opt-in addendum. Retraining addenda should specify compensation (credits or fee) and data handling assurances (KMS/HSM controls, deletion windows).

Proposed contract language (suggestion to insert as new subsection X.4):
"Customer Rights to Outputs: Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, and distribute Outputs produced by the Service. Redwood retains the right to use Outputs and related metadata in de-identified and aggregated form solely to provide, maintain, and improve the Service, subject to the restrictions in this Agreement.

Telemetry and Training: Redwood may collect technical telemetry and usage metadata (e.g., request latencies, error codes, token counts) to operate the Service; such telemetry will not be used for model retraining and will be retained no longer than thirty (30) days. Any use of Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or modify model weights ("Retraining") shall require a separate written agreement executed by both parties."

Operational next steps:
- I will produce a clean redline against BrightCo_MSA_redlines_v1 with the language above by 6/13 EOD.
- If BrightCo prefers explicit "retrain credits" as currency, we can map that in the order form; otherwise, default will be a commercial negotiation.

Emma — does that compromise reflect BrightCo's risk profile? If you sign off we can push to procurement for DocuSign.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
